title: Microsoft DEF 14A definitive proxy statement (est.) — the document that carries the 2026 shareholder-proposal slate and confirms the meeting date
source: EST: NO ANNOUNCED DATE EXISTS FOR A PROXY FILING — the SEC never schedules one and Microsoft never pre-announces one, so this entry is an INFERENCE FROM MEASURED CADENCE and is labelled estimate for exactly that reason, permanently, until the filing itself appears. Written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the single prior proposal (proposals/msft-def14a-2026-10-22.from-msft-annual-meeting-2026-12-08.json, now inert) and then RE-DERIVED the date from two INDEPENDENT anchors rather than inheriting one. Both anchors were built from data.sec.gov's submissions index for CIK 0000789019, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 184,335 + 307,323 bytes), covering all eighteen DEF 14A filings 2008-2025 and all eighteen matching Form 10-K filings. ANCHOR A (meeting lag): DEF 14A -> annual meeting is 47 days median over 2018-2025 (n=8, sd 2.20, range 43-50); applied to the confirmed meeting date 2026-12-08 it gives 2026-10-22, a Thursday, the weekday of four of the last five filings. ANCHOR B (10-K lag, independent of the meeting date entirely): Form 10-K -> DEF 14A is 84 days median over the last five years (sd 5.07); applied to the FY2026 10-K filed 2026-07-29 it gives 2026-10-21. The two anchors agree to within ONE DAY while sharing no input, which is why this entry is dated 2026-10-22 rather than earlier in the window. Anchor A is used as the point estimate because it is 2.3x tighter (sd 2.20 vs 5.07). HONEST WINDOW: 2026-10-19..2026-10-26, being Anchor A's full n=8 lag range; a weaker third anchor (the proxy lands a median 7.5 days BEFORE the FY-Q1 print in 17 of the last 18 years) reads off the ESTIMATE 2026-10-27 print and so only widens caution toward the earlier edge, never narrows it. Treat this entry as that window with a point estimate at its centre, never as a scheduled release. TIMING, WHICH THE DATE ALONE HIDES: sixteen of the last eighteen proxies were accepted by EDGAR AFTER the 16:00 ET close (median acceptance 16:16 ET; the exceptions are 2018 at 14:04 ET and 2022 at 09:05 ET), so the first session that can price this filing is normally the day AFTER the date in this entry — for a 2026-10-22 filing, Friday 2026-10-23. PROMOTION CRITERION: the filing appearing on data.sec.gov's CIK0000789019 submissions feed as form DEF 14A flips this to confirmed on a SEC: prefix, on its ACTUAL date. Verified 2026-09-09 that no 2026 DEF 14A exists yet — the most recent is 2025-10-21, and the submissions index runs through 2026-09-08
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-09 (D-43) — docs/research/events/msft-def14a-2026-10-22.md. THE CALL IS STAND ASIDE AT EVERY HORIZON, and it is a measurement, not a prior. This lane's own n=18 event study (2008-2025, MSFT minus QQQ, Yahoo adjusted closes via scripts/research/market-data.mjs) anchored on THE FIRST SESSION THAT COULD ACTUALLY PRICE THE FILING rather than on the filing date: mean +0.21pp, median -0.15pp, win 7/18, sd 1.11. Drop 2008-09-30 (the TARP-vote crash rebound, +3.84pp, nothing to do with a proxy) and the cell is mean -0.00pp, median -0.15pp, win 6/17, sd 0.67, t=-0.01, full range [-0.81pp, +1.52pp]. THE ANCHOR CORRECTION MATTERS AND IS THIS LANE'S OWN FINDING: measuring the filing DATE instead measures a session in which the document was not yet public 16 times out of 18. THE D->D+5 CELL IS AN EARNINGS WINDOW IN DISGUISE: it looks like +1.07pp mean, but the proxy is filed a median 7.5 days before the FY-Q1 print, so in 6 of 18 years the five-session window CONTAINS the print (contaminated n=6 mean +2.24pp vs clean n=12 mean +0.49pp); drop the print years and 2008 and it is -0.14pp, win 3/11, t=-0.42. NO PLAYBOOK FIRES, and the after-close acceptance time makes that structural rather than incidental: an overnight gap is the only expression route for a 16:16 ET filing, and S4 (overnight-only) is KILLED on MSFT specifically (trade-playbooks.md), with intraday-edges.mjs putting the overnight bar at 34.8% of MSFT's daily volatility on +0.048% mean and a 2.4bps break-even. WHAT THE DOCUMENT ACTUALLY CARRIES, read from the 2025 proxy direct (sec.gov, HTTP 200, 2,430,412 bytes): four management proposals (12 directors, say-on-pay, auditor ratification, stock plan) and six shareholder proposals, ALL of them AI/data/human-rights risk-audit requests filed by advocacy groups. Not one is a financial disclosure. The proxy is where the AI-governance headlines live and where the guidance does not. IT REMAINS THE DATE FALSIFIER for msft-annual-meeting-2026-12-08: a proxy naming any meeting date other than 2026-12-08 breaks that entry's 8-for-8 10-K-vs-proxy record. KIND: 'sector' because KINDS in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs has no company-governance slot, same as the parent entry.
